title: Sell-side global markets functional architecture (trade lifecycle view)

stages.name: Onboarding
stages.purpose: Make a client legally, credit and operationally ready to trade.
stages.value: Cost sits here: onboarding time delays first trade and revenue; credit and documentation set the capital each client consumes.

components.name: Client Onboarding Workflow
components.does: Orchestrates entity due diligence, document collection, approvals and account opening across desks

components.name: KYC and Sanctions Screening
components.does: Identity, beneficial ownership, sanctions and adverse media checks with periodic refresh

components.name: Client Categorisation Register
components.does: Records retail, professional or eligible counterparty status and regulatory classifications per entity

components.name: Counterparty Credit Approval
components.does: Rates the counterparty and sets credit appetite, limits and collateral terms before trading

components.name: Master Agreement Repository
components.does: Holds ISDA, CSA, GMRA, GMSLA and give-up terms as structured, queryable elections

components.name: Standing Settlement Instructions
components.does: Stores client and market settlement instructions by asset class, currency and place

components.name: Account and Access Setup
components.does: Creates trading accounts, desk mappings and client electronic platform entitlements

stages.name: Origination
stages.purpose: Win secondary-market client business: coverage, quoting, structuring and suitability (primary issuance out of scope)
stages.value: Margin sits here: bid-offer spread on flow and structuring margin on bespoke products.

components.name: Sales CRM and Coverage
components.does: Tracks client coverage, interactions, revenue attribution and call reports

components.name: Axes and Indications
components.does: Publishes dealer axes and indications of interest to clients and platforms

components.name: RFQ and Quote Management
components.does: Receives requests for quote, prices them and manages quote acceptance across channels

components.name: Bond and Credit RFQ
components.does: Auto-prices and responds to multi-dealer platform RFQs for bonds and credit

components.name: FX Streaming Prices
components.does: Streams executable FX prices to clients and platforms with client-tiered spreads

components.name: Single-Dealer Platform and Client APIs
components.does: Gives clients branded web and API access to prices, RFQ, orders, post-trade status and analytics

components.name: Structuring and Pricing Models
components.does: Designs and prices structured and exotic trades using approved models

components.name: Suitability and Appropriateness
components.does: Checks product fit to client categorisation, knowledge and target market before dealing

components.name: New Product Approval
components.does: Governs new products: risk, legal, operational and booking readiness sign-off

stages.name: Execution
stages.purpose: Execute orders and quotes with control and best execution.
stages.value: Margin sits here: internalisation, execution quality and electronic scale; cost sits in venue fees and errors.

components.name: Order Management System
components.does: Captures, validates and manages client and principal orders through their lifecycle

components.name: Pre-Trade Risk Controls
components.does: Applies price, size, credit and market-access checks before orders leave

components.name: Client DMA Gateway
components.does: Gives clients direct market access and algo order entry over FIX

components.name: Execution and Smart Routing
components.does: Routes orders across venues and liquidity pools seeking best execution

components.name: Algorithmic Execution Engine
components.does: Runs execution algorithms and basket trades under algo governance controls

components.name: FX Aggregation and Internalisation
components.does: Aggregates external FX liquidity, internalises client flow and hedges residual risk

components.name: Trader Workstation
components.does: Trader desktop for blotters, quotes, orders, voice trade capture and intraday risk

components.name: Trader Position Management
components.does: Maintains real-time desk positions, inventory and hedging needs

components.name: Venue Connectivity Gateways
components.does: Connects to exchanges, MTFs and OTFs using FIX or native protocols

stages.name: Confirmation
stages.purpose: Book, allocate, confirm and agree every trade with the client.
stages.value: Cost sits here: breaks, late confirmations and manual affirmation drive operational risk and headcount.

components.name: Trade Capture and Booking
components.does: Books executed trades to books and UK, EU or US legal entities, including back-to-back and intercompany legs

components.name: Trade Enrichment
components.does: Adds settlement instructions, fees, identifiers and regulatory flags to booked trades

components.name: Commissions, Fees and Client Billing
components.does: Calculates commissions and clearing, custody and financing fees; invoices clients; reconciles exchange, CCP and broker fees and passes on penalties

components.name: Allocation and Affirmation
components.does: Splits block trades into client allocations and drives same-day affirmation

components.name: Trade Matching Utility
components.does: Third-party central matching of institutional trade details and confirmations

groups.name: OTC and Structured Confirmation and Lifecycle

components.name: OTC Confirmation Matching
components.does: Generates, matches and chases OTC derivative and FX confirmations within deadlines
components.msg: FpML confirmation; CDM event model; MT300/MT305 (FX confirmations)

components.name: Portfolio Reconciliation and Disputes
components.does: Reconciles OTC portfolios with counterparties and manages valuation disputes

components.name: Lifecycle Event Processing
components.does: Processes resets, exercises, novations, terminations and compression results

components.name: Structured Products Lifecycle

stages.name: Risk and Reporting
stages.purpose: Measure risk and P&L and report every trade to regulators and markets.

components.name: Trading Risk Engine
components.does: Calculates sensitivities, VaR and stress results for trading books

components.name: P&L and Product Control
components.does: Produces daily P&L, attribution and book sign-off for trading desks

components.name: Independent Price Verification

components.name: Transaction Reporting

components.name: Derivatives Trade Reporting

components.name: Pre- and Post-Trade Transparency

stages.name: Clearing
stages.purpose: Novate eligible trades to CCPs and manage margin and netting.
stages.value: Cost sits here: margin funding, CCP fees and capital; client clearing earns fees.

stages.name: Settlement
stages.purpose: Exchange securities and cash with finality, on time.

assumptions: Archetype: a global bank's markets division (sales and trading only) with UK, EU and US legal entities, dealing as principal and agent across EQ, FI, FX and DR.
Out of scope: primary issuance (ECM/DCM), research production, corporate and retail banking, treasury ALM beyond trading funding, and agentic AI.

The bank runs its own custody business (S7), so custody components are internal; CSDs, ICSDs, CCPs, CLS, agent banks, trade repositories, triparty agents, data vendors and the messaging network are third-party run and appear as external parties. Four FMI touchpoints (C28, C41, C49, C50) are drawn in-stage to show the flow; they are the same parties as X13, X04, X05 and X07.
Stages follow the owner's 10-stage Trade Flow Value Chain. A trade does not pass every stage: FX skips custody, OTC uncleared skips CCP clearing, listed derivatives skip CSD settlement.
Asset-class tags: EQ equities, FI fixed income (rates and credit), FX, DR derivatives (OTC and listed); ALL when common to all four.
external=true means usually run by a third party. The bank keeps oversight through C96 Third-Party and FMI Oversight, C51 Agent Bank Management and C95 Operational Resilience.

Regulatory reporting is produced in S4 (transaction, derivative, transparency) and S8 (SFTR), and controlled centrally in P6 (C91). Surveillance and the control room sit in P6 as second-line functions.
Cross-reference fields are left blank where no honest match exists. BIAN names are labels from v10, not structure; several are closest fit.
FIX names are FIX Latest MsgType names; iso20022 lists business areas only, not message versions; swift_mt numbers are unverified analyst knowledge.
Links are illustrative key flows in three threads; the real integration estate is far denser and most components read from the platform.
No vendor product names and no statistics. Regimes marked not verified were not checked against the source for this draft and should be validated before external use.
Office assignment is a convention; banks differ (for example some run prime services or clearing under Middle Office).

families.BIAN: Strong: Party Lifecycle Management, Counterparty Risk, Customer Agreement, Customer Access Entitlement.
families.CALM: Services and databases; client is an actor.
families.FIX: SettlementInstructions and SettlementInstructionRequest for standing instructions only; onboarding itself is not a FIX process.
families.FpML_CDM: CDM legal agreements model for CSA elections.
families.ISO20022: Not used here in this map (acmt applies to custody accounts in S7).
families.other: KYC/AML and MiFID categorisation (unverified); no data standard for KYC files.

families.BIAN: Good: Customer Relationship Management, Quote Management, Market Making, Suitability Checking, Product Design; Trading Models is closest fit.
families.CALM: Engagement services; platforms are ecosystem externals.
families.FIX: IOI, QuoteRequest, Quote, QuoteResponse; NewOrderSingle through the client channel.
families.FpML_CDM: Product model for structured and OTC trades.

families.BIAN: Strong: Market Order, Market Order Execution, Program Trading, eTrading Workbench, Trader Position Operations.
families.ISO20022: None (setr is fund and securities trade initiation, used little on sell-side execution).

families.BIAN: Good: Order Allocation, Trade Confirmation Matching, Commissions. No domain for booking, enrichment or structured products lifecycle.
families.CALM: Services; matching utility is an ecosystem.
families.FpML_CDM: Core: FpML confirmation; CDM product and event models for lifecycle and structured products.
families.ISO20022: Not mapped (setr/fxtr confirmations exist but were not checked at message level).
families.other: T+1 affirmation (verified dates); EMIR confirmation timelines (unverified).

families.BIAN: Partial: Regulatory Reporting, Trade and Price Reporting (fits public trade publication here), Trading Book Oversight, Financial Instrument Valuation, Market Risk Models.
families.FpML_CDM: FpML reporting views; CDM event model feeds derivative reporting.
families.other: MiFIR Art 26, EMIR Refit, CFTC Part 45 verified; Part 43, SBSR, UK MiFIR, SEC CAT and FINRA TRACE unverified.

families.BIAN: Partial: Trade Clearing, Credit and Margin Management, Collateral Allocation Management. No domain for client clearing or compression.
families.CALM: CCP is an ecosystem; bank side services.
families.ISO20022: secl for securities clearing only (derivative and futures clearing use FIXML, FpML or CCP-specific interfaces); colr margin calls.
families.other: ISDA SIMM verified; UMR scope and CCP margin models unverified.

families.BIAN: Good: Trade Settlement, Securities Fails Processing, Sub Custodian Agreement.
families.CALM: CSDs and PvP system are ecosystems; Swift is a network.
families.FIX: None mapped; SettlementInstructions is a standing instruction message and sits with SSIs in S0.
families.SWIFT_MT: MT540-548 (unverified numbers); Swift set no securities MT end date (verified).
families.other: EU CSDR settlement discipline, US/UK/EU T+1 verified; CLS verified.

families.BIAN: Good: Securities Position Keeping, Custody Administration, Corporate Action, Customer Tax Handling. No client-asset or income domain.
families.other: CASS and 15c3-3 unverified (segregation controls sit in P7); no global standard for tax reclaim files.

families.BIAN: Partial: Stock Lending and Repos, Credit and Margin Management, Regulatory Reporting. No domain for locates, TRS or rehypothecation.
families.FpML_CDM: CDM securities lending and repo representation; FpML/CDM equity swaps.
families.other: SFTR verified; Reg SHO, CASS reuse unverified.

families.BIAN: Good: Information Provider Operation and Administration, Market Data Switch Operation, Market Information Management.
families.other: No open standard for licence and usage reporting.

families.BIAN: Good for reference data, limits, collateral, treasury, accounting, gateway, archive, compliance; none for lineage, best execution, reconciliation, surveillance or client money.
families.CALM: ldap for identity; networks for event streaming; databases and services for controls.
families.FIX: SecurityDefinition for instruments; PositionReport for CCP statements; session layer at the gateway.
families.FpML_CDM: CDM product, event and eligible-collateral models.
families.ISO20022: reda, colr, camt, pacs, auth, semt, sese, seev.
families.SWIFT_MT: MT54x/MT56x translation, MT950, MT535/536, MT527/558 (unverified numbers); payments moved to pacs/camt in November 2025 (verified).
families.other: PS21/3 and DORA verified; CASS, BCBS 239, FRTB, SA-CCR, Volcker, LEI, MAR control room unverified.

BIAN.note: All names copied from BIAN v10 value chain view; several are closest fit.

CALM.note: Every component has a CALM 1.1 node type.

FIX.note: MsgType names checked against a FIX Latest dictionary.

FpML_CDM.note: Family level (FpML; CDM product, event, legal, collateral, repo); not message level.

ISO20022.note: Business areas only; message identifiers not checked.

regs.note: See standards list for verified flag per regime.

gaps: No open standard for KYC due-diligence data or onboarding workflow

No BIAN domain for KYC screening, trade booking/enrichment, front-to-back reconciliation, control room, structured products lifecycle, single-dealer platform, surveillance, best execution, client clearing, compression, locates, TRS, rehypothecation, client assets, data lineage or valuation adjustments
No messaging standard for pre-trade risk controls, internal P&L, product control or IPV
No open standard for market data licence and usage reporting
No common standard for tax reclaim submissions
Operational resilience, third-party oversight and conduct have regulation but no data or messaging standard
ISO 20022 for sell-side execution (setr) is little used; FIX dominates
FpML/CDM cover OTC derivatives, repo, lending and collateral, not cash equity or bond settlement
